newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia elected to U.N. Human Rights Committee.
newsitem.headline: Colombia elected to U.N. Human Rights Committee.

text.p: Colombia, which has one of the worst human rights records in the Americas, has been elected to serve on a U.N. committee that monitors global human rights, government officials said on Friday.
A brief statement from the foreign ministry said Colombia was elected to the 18-member U.N. Human Rights Committee on Thursday.

The committee, which oversees reports from countries that are parties to an international covenant on civil and political rights, has a far more limited role than the Geneva-based United Nations Human Rights Commission.
The government agreed in August to allow Jose Ayala-Lasso, the U.N. high commissioner for human rights, to open a permanent office in Colombia to monitor its own human rights situation.
Colombia -- which has been at war with leftist guerrillas for more than three decades -- has one of the highest murder and kidnapping rates in the world.
Gunmen from the left and right have killed with impunity in the country for years, and rights groups have repeatedly criticised the government's inability to curb abuses by the Colombian military.
